text.p: Dutch steel and aluminium group Hoogovens on Thursday repeated a forecast that net profit from ordinary operations in the second half 1996 would be around the first half's 142 million guilders.

"Hoogovens maintains its forecast on the results...this means the net result on ordinary activities in the second half will remain at the same level as in the first, when that result amounted to NLG 142 million," Chairman Maarten van Veen said.
The company said in August that it expected ordinary net earnings to stabilise in the second half as demand for aluminium and steel products picked up.
Van Veen told reporters that demand for steel had picked up in Europe compared with the start of the year, but prices for rolled and extruded aluminium products remained under pressure.
